relation: Distinct canonical Brain-registry storage defect; commercial cron #4215 remains separately unresolved
failure_pattern: New brain_observe_failure occurrence overwrites registry.evidence, while two agent formats encode the same job46/runid and inflate the raw occurrence count.

observed_evidence.security: SECURITY DEFINER, anon/authenticated cannot EXECUTE, service_role can EXECUTE

root_cause: Registry current evidence is replaced wholesale on observe; deduplication's only identity is caller-supplied exact occurrence_id, not normalized physical provider cron job/run.
proposed_fix: Preserve old registry evidence in place; maintain raw append-only occurrences for new details; normalize known cron occurrence-ID aliases by jobid and runid and serialize concurrent writers with a transaction-scoped advisory lock; reject conflicting provider status or exact-ID mismatched hashes.
prevention: All agents use one canonical provider event identity and a single Brain RPC before writing a new recovery occurrence.
Do not overwrite verified or promoted evidence with an observation's latest raw JSON; the raw ledger holds new events.
Distinguish raw historical occurrences from normalized unique provider events; retain old raw records unmodified.
Run transaction-only positive/negative regression before creating a protected release; preserve service-role-only permissions.
Do not infer production recovery from source CI, a draft PR, or old commercial snapshot rows.

Source-code edits containing JavaScript replacement tokens such as $' must use a replacement callback, not a replacement template; a temporary malformed migration write was corrected from its immutable previous commit before PR creation.
release_gates: Representative service-role test on appropriate isolated provider preview without copied customer PII
Production RPC ACL and idempotent occurrence readback
